facts.F3: The plaintiff was in Hospital from 23rd September, 1973 to 20th October, 1973.
facts.F4: The plaintiff's injuries on admission consisted of a 2 inch haematoma over the right forehead, 2 ½ inch laceration over the left parietal region of the scalp, 1 ½ inch laceration over the left cheek near the lips, 2 inch laceration over the front of the left thigh and a ¼ inch laceration over the front of the left shin.
facts.F5: The plaintiff was diagnosed as suffering from contusion of the brain.
facts.F6: The main brunt of the injury appeared to have been borne by the left side of the skull and brain.
facts.F7: The plaintiff now suffers permanently from total blindness of the left eye.
facts.F8: The plaintiff also suffers from mild headaches which are getting less frequent and less severe.
facts.F9: For some months after the accident there was a weakness of the right lower limb which gradually became milder until in 1978 any weakness had disappeared.
facts.F10: The plaintiff was a construction worker in the New Territories before the accident.
facts.F11: The plaintiff was employed as a regular and not as a casual worker.
facts.F12: The plaintiff helped to build village houses and worked on smaller rather than major projects.
facts.F13: The plaintiff's duties included plastering, aligning and erecting brick walls, mixing cement and related work.
facts.F14: The plaintiff's work regularly involved working on scaffolding.
facts.F15: The plaintiff had been involved in this type of work for 3 ½ years before the accident.
facts.F16: At the date of the accident the plaintiff earned $60 per day.
facts.F17: The plaintiff was then working 26 days a month earning a monthly wage of $1,560.
facts.F18: The plaintiff's current rate for doing the same work as the plaintiff did before the accident is $75 per day.

facts.F1: The Appellant was appointed as the piling contractor for a site preparation project at 12-14 Marigold Road, Kowloon.
facts.F2: The Appellant was notified to the Building Authority via Form 16 on 25th June 1987.
facts.F3: Two charges were brought against the Appellant before the Disciplinary Board, but the second charge was abandoned.
facts.F4: The remaining charge alleged that the Appellant deviated from the approved piling plan in a material way, specifically with regards to pile H10.
facts.F5: Pile H10 was not driven through the boulder encountered and was found to be significantly shorter than specified, measuring only 1.37 meters instead of the required 16.8 meters.
facts.F6: The Appellant's site foreman, Mr. Chan, was not present on site when the piling work for H10 was completed and did not supervise the work.
facts.F7: Mr. Chan relied on the reports and graphs submitted by the site staff and did not detect any irregularities.
facts.F8: The Appellant was not aware of the material deviation until it was discovered during excavation work in mid-November 1987.
facts.F9: It is generally accepted practice in the building trade for a small site to be supervised by a foreman who is not a qualified engineer.

reference_issues: Whether the Disciplinary Board erred in law in failing to appreciate the true nature of section 13(1) negligence.
Whether there was sufficient evidence to establish the Appellant's negligence under section 13(1).
Whether the Appellant's site foreman's negligence can be attributed to the Appellant.

claim: The plaintiff sues the defendant for the return of their deposit in the sum of $100,000 paid under a contract in the Chinese language, entered into with the defendant for the supply of a second-hand crane.
requested_remedy: The plaintiff sues the defendant for the return of their deposit in the sum of $100,000 paid under a contract in the Chinese language, entered into with the defendant for the supply of a second-hand crane.

facts.F1: The contract between the plaintiff and the defendant was in Chinese.
facts.F2: The contract provided for the payment of a deposit in the sum of HK$100,000.
facts.F3: The contract stipulated that the deposit was to be paid upon signing of the contract.
facts.F4: The defendant demanded a deposit of up to 20% of the purchase price of $880,000, but eventually came down to $100,000, representing 11.36%.
facts.F5: The plaintiff conceded on liability with reference to the merchantability of the crane.
facts.F6: The defendant counterclaims for damages, having maintained that the $100,000 deposit had been rightly forfeited.
facts.F7: The contract provided that if the purchaser had not accepted delivery as scheduled, the purchaser shall pay HK$1,000 per day as rental to the seller.
facts.F8: The term 'rental' in the contract was later clarified to mean 'warehouse charges'.
facts.F9: The defendant's policy was to take a deposit of 20 to 25% from buyers of small machines and 10 to 20% deposit on a large machine, such as the crane ordered in this case.
facts.F10: The defendant's Assistant Sales Manager, Mr. Tam, explained that a deposit was normally demanded or taken, not on any percentage basis, but in a lump sum, as in this case eventually at $100,000.
facts.F11: The gross profit for the crane to be sold by the defendant to the plaintiff was about 10% of the purchase price.
facts.F12: Any rejection would lead to losses to the defendant in terms of banking interest on the remaining balance of the purchase price, which would continue to run, subject probably to the risk of losing the banking charges of some $60,000 odd which would have had to be incurred by the time of resale, storage charges until resale, the likelihood of a resale at a loss and the possibility of reducing the company's turnover profit.
facts.F13: The parties negotiated at arm's length and general terms were discussed.
facts.F14: A manufacturer's report was produced late in the proceedings.

reference_issues: Whether the provision for the payment of $100,000 deposit was a penal provision or whether it was a pre-estimate of loss enforceable by the defendant on the plaintiff's default.
Whether the evidence given in these proceedings is sufficient to confer on the defendant the benefit of the provision for payment of deposit, implicitly forfeitable upon default.

facts.F1: The Defendant applied for Comprehensive Social Security Assistance (“CSSA”), a scheme of public subsidies to be considered and granted by the Social Welfare Department (“SWD”), and she was interviewed by a SWD officer on 2006-04-06.
facts.F2: The Defendant declared that she only had cash of $3,000 and money in her Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (“HSBC”) bank account totalling $12,054.53.
facts.F3: Between 2007 and 2012, the Defendant was invited to attend 12 periodic reviews, and she was interviewed by SWD officers, during which she declared that she had two bank accounts from HSBC and Bank of China (Hong Kong) Limited (“BOC”) with cash deposited in those accounts ranging from $4,438.29 to $28,629.18.
facts.F4: In a review interview held on 2013-09-19, the Defendant revealed that she owned a Bank of Communication bank account, which had not been disclosed to SWD before, and that she was willing to make repayment to SWD and to cease from collecting CSSA subsidies from SWD.
facts.F5: SWD investigated on the Defendant's financial background and confirmed that at the time of the application made by the Defendant on 2006-03-06, the Defendant and her family had total assets of over $121,374.01, which exceeded the level of CSSA asset limit for the size of the Defendant's family at the time.
facts.F6: The Defendant was found to have made false declarations to SWD officers during the CSSA application and periodic review interviews held between 2006-04-06 and 2013-09-18, resulting in her being overpaid with CSSA totalling $332,232.52 by SWD.
facts.F7: The Defendant made full repayment to SWD and was arrested on 2016-06-13, admitting to the facts of the case under caution.

facts.F9: The Defendant had developed a strong Christian faith and her parental relationship had significantly improved as the present case progressed.
facts.F10: The Defendant engaged in voluntary community work.
facts.F11: A sum of over $240,000 was considered a significant amount deserving a sentence of over 24 months.
